html:
The Herero and Nama genocide was the destruction of the Herero and Nama peoples by the German army in German South West Africa between 1904 and 1908.

The Herero rose in January 1904 against land seizures and abuse. After defeating them at the Waterberg in August, General Lothar von Trotha drove them into the Omaheke desert and ordered that any Herero found in German territory be shot. Many died of thirst. The Nama under Hendrik Witbooi rose that October. Survivors were held in concentration camps, such as Shark Island near Lüderitz, where most died.

About 80 percent of the Herero and half of the Nama are thought to have died. Germany recognised the killings as genocide in 2021. Their land went to settlers, which shapes land politics in Namibia still.
sum: The Herero and Nama genocide was the destruction of the Herero and Nama peoples by the German army in German South West Africa between 1904 and 1908.
